In 1959 the American company Esso found a large oil field at Zelten in the Sirte basin of Libya. Exports began in 1961.

Libya was then one of the poorest countries in the world, living on aid and rent from American and British bases. Oil, close to Europe and light and easy to refine, changed it within a decade. Under King Idris the money went largely to a small elite.

After 1969 Gaddafi forced the oil companies to pay more, and Libya led the push that raised oil prices before the 1973 crisis. Oil paid for the Great Man-Made River, free housing and his foreign adventures. It is still almost all of Libya's income.
